extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI (self-assessment), or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (e.g., biometric identification), the provider may choose internal control or notified-body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied; Annex VII (notified body) assessment is mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems, while most other high-risk systems can use the Annex VI self-assessment route.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product-safety legislation listed in Section A of Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery), the provider must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies also ensuring compliance with AI-specific requirements.

Under Article 43, for the conformity assessment referred to in Annex VII the provider may choose any notified body, except that where the high-risk AI system is to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or by Union institutions/bodies/offices/agencies, the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body.
Substantial modifications to a high-risk AI system require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority to authorise, by derogation from Article 43, the placing on the market or putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems for a limited period, for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life/health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets, without the standard conformity assessment.

Annex VII, point 4.5, provides that a notified body may, where necessary and after other verification means are exhausted, be granted access to the training and trained models of the AI system, including relevant parameters, subject to IP and confidentiality protections.

Notified bodies performing Annex VII assessments verify that the provider's quality management system complies with Article 17 and examine technical documentation to assess compliance with the essential requirements in Chapter III, Section 2.
The Commission may adopt delegated acts under Article 43(5) and Article 97 to update Annex VI and Annex VII conformity assessment procedures in light of technical progress.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes administrative rules on identification numbers and lists of notified bodies designated under the AI Act.

A draft Council document lists AIP codes defining the scope of designation of conformity assessment bodies notified under Article 30 of the (related) Regulation, corresponding to categories of AI systems under Annex I of the AI Act.

A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836 / 2025/0359 (COD)) proposes creating a new Annex XIV listing categories of AI systems for the NANDO notified-body information system, and amending Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements into aviation safety regulation.
As of March 2026, no AI Act-specific notified bodies had been designated; designation processes were reported as ongoing across member states with limited capacity.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act according to a medical-device-focused industry guide.
An industry guide states that notified bodies designated under the AI Act will begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments only 'post-2026'.

For comparison, under the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), as of late June 2026 zero notified bodies had been designated in the Commission's NANDO database, with a target of 11 December 2026 for sufficient capacity.
As of October 2025, the NANDO system listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies (medical devices regulations, not AI Act-specific).

A news/legal-analysis source dated 15 September 2026 reports that the final text agreed in September 2026 moved the start date for AI Act Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 August 2029, replacing an earlier reported date of 2 December 2027, citing unreadiness of harmonised standards and notified bodies.

A legal-analysis source dated 22 September 2026 states that Annex III high-risk obligations apply from 2 August 2029 following a 'second amendment' of Article 113, replacing a 2 December 2027 date set by the 'AI Omnibus', and that until then providers do not need notified-body conformity assessment for these systems.

A client alert dated 29 September 2026 states that EU institutions have deferred application of AI Act high-risk requirements for Annex III systems to 2 August 2029, to allow time for harmonised standards and designation of the first notified bodies.

A separate industry source (undated, SaaS-focused) refers to an 'August 2, 2026' deadline by which SaaS providers must issue an EU Declaration of Conformity, implying high-risk obligations applying on that date rather than 2029.
Another industry compliance guide states 'August 2026: High-risk AI obligations fully apply' as the key deadline, and refers to notified bodies being designated under the AI Act only 'post-2026'.
A compliance-automation blog (dated context March 2026) states 'the August 2026 deadline isn't moving' for engaging a notified body.

The original 2021 Commission proposal text of Article 43 (pre-adoption draft) described conformity assessment options for Annex III point 1 systems involving harmonised standards, common specifications and notified-body or internal-control procedures, differing in detail from the final adopted Article 43 text.

It is unclear whether the Commission proposal COM(2025) 836 (creating Annex XIV for NANDO) has been formally adopted, and if so, on what date and in what final form.

The exact legal status and date of the amendment to Article 113 (postponing Annex III obligations to 2 August 2029) is not clearly documented by an authoritative primary source (e.g., Official Journal citation); only secondary legal-analysis blogs report this.

It is unclear how the conflicting 'August 2026' deadline language in several industry blogs (sources 22, 24, 30) should be reconciled with the later-reported 2029 postponement — whether these sources are simply outdated or refer to different categories of obligations (e.g., GPAI vs Annex III high-risk).

No source provides a definitive, current list of specific named notified bodies (with identification numbers) actually designated for the AI Act, despite Article 35 establishing the mechanism for publishing such lists.

The relationship between Annex I Section A product-safety regimes' existing notified bodies (e.g., under MDR/IVDR, machinery, aviation) and new AI Act-specific notified-body designations is not fully clarified — sources suggest integration is still pending (e.g., source 9's amendment to Regulation 2018/1139).

It is not clear what specific criteria or timeline govern the designation of market surveillance authorities as notified bodies for law-enforcement/immigration/asylum high-risk systems under Article 43(1).
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act and the Status of Notified Body Designations

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes a two-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems—internal control and notified-body assessment—with the applicable route depending on the system's category and existing sectoral regulation (medium–high confidence). However, as of early-to-mid 2026, no notified bodies appear to have been formally designated for AI Act-specific assessments, and sources disagree sharply on when Annex III high-risk obligations actually take legal effect, ranging from August 2026 to August 2029 (low–medium confidence, contested).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two main routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control (self-assessment) under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). For Annex III point 1 systems (e.g., biometric identification), the choice between routes depends on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied, with notified-body assessment reportedly mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems (low confidence) ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). For high-risk systems already covered by existing EU product-safety legislation in Annex I Section A (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

Under Article 43, providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except that the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body for systems used by law enforcement, immigration/asylum authorities, or EU institutions (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Substantial modifications generally require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to authorise placing high-risk systems on the market without standard conformity assessment, for a limited period, on grounds of public security, health, environmental or infrastructural protection (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Annex VII, point 4.5, allows notified bodies, as a last resort, access to training and trained models including parameters, subject to IP/confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
Article 35 establishes administrative rules for identification numbers and public lists of notified bodies designated under the AI Act (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)). Despite this framework, no source confirms any notified body had actually been designated as of March–April 2026 (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [AI Act Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). A draft Council document discusses a detailed "AIP code" scheme defining designation scope for conformity assessment bodies, suggesting administrative groundwork is underway (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). A separate Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) proposes a new Annex XIV for the NANDO notified-body database and integration with aviation safety rules, though its adoption status is unclear (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)). For comparison, under the adjacent Cyber Resilience Act, zero notified bodies were listed in NANDO as of late June 2026 (low confidence) ([CyberCertLabs](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026)), while NANDO listed 51 MDR and 19 IVDR notified bodies as of October 2025 for unrelated medical-device regimes (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources conflict significantly on the applicable deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations. ## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes a two-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems—internal control and notified-body assessment—with the applicable route depending on the system's category and existing sectoral regulation (medium–high confidence). However, as of early-to-mid 2026, no notified bodies appear to have been formally designated for AI Act-specific assessments, and sources disagree sharply on when Annex III high-risk obligations actually take legal effect, ranging from August 2026 to August 2029 (low–medium confidence, contested).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two main routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control (self-assessment) under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). For Annex III point 1 systems (e.g., biometric identification), the choice between routes depends on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied, with notified-body assessment reportedly mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems (low confidence) ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). For high-risk systems already covered by existing EU product-safety legislation in Annex I Section A (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

Under Article 43, providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except that the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body for systems used by law enforcement, immigration/asylum authorities, or EU institutions (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Substantial modifications generally require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to authorise placing high-risk systems on the market without standard conformity assessment, for a limited period, on grounds of public security, health, environmental or infrastructural protection (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Annex VII, point 4.5, allows notified bodies, as a last resort, access to training and trained models including parameters, subject to IP/confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
Article 35 establishes administrative rules for identification numbers and public lists of notified bodies designated under the AI Act (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)).
